title: Louisiana shut my trading bot down mid-run. Here's the full board, good and bad.
author: No-Limit-4804
selftext:
Three weeks ago I posted here about Trader's B, the bot store I built, with its record public at tradersb.com. This is the update, and it starts with the bad news.

Live trading is paused. On November 12 the Louisiana Attorney General sued Kalshi, and a court order bars event contracts in Louisiana without a state gaming license. I am in Louisiana, so my bot stopped placing live trades on November 17 and it stays stopped until that clears. A hearing is set for November 30. I would rather tell you that here than have you find a quiet board and wonder.

The good news is the pause is only mine. We have three signups so far, and the customers in other states are not under the Louisiana order. Their bots are still trading, and they are doing decent. Only the Louisiana side is sitting out.

The call board itself, scored on the last 325 calls over 21 days (1,992 BTC windows tracked): taker +1.24 cents a contract, 56% won, +$4.04 total. Maker at max price filled all 325 and did a little better, +1.57 cents, +$5.11. The strict post-only book is the honest downside: it only filled 231 of 325 and lost, minus 4.74 cents a contract, minus $10.95. And the live money record from before the pause is still underwater overall. The board shows all of it, including the losing book, and it stays up while we are paused.

What is still running: the paper lanes, the feeds, and the research, so the board keeps learning while the lawyers do their thing. Sizing is now one contract flat, cut down from percentage sizing after the numbers said the small account could not carry it.

Pricing has not changed: $9 for the first 15 days, then $29, $59, or $119 a month. Nobody's funds are held by us. Every customer trades their own Kalshi account with their own keys.

My question for this sub is the same one I asked last time, and I still go back and forth on it: does showing the losing book and the zero progress during a forced pause build trust, or does it just look broken? It stays up either way. I am asking because I want to know how it reads from the outside.

comments.author: QuanTradin
comments.body: the post-only book losing while taker and maker-at-max both made money says a lot. a resting order that only fills 231 of 325 mostly gets filled on the windows where price was already moving through it, so the misses aren't random, they're the good windows it never got into. more calls usually won't close that gap.

comments.author: travelingthrwaway
comments.body: Is there any indication that Kalshi will block your platform in the future due to your location in Louisiana?
